request.query: Difference of distinct integer multivariate polynomials with coordinate degree bounds and coefficients between zero and B is nonzero with same degree bounds and absolute coefficients at most B

items.informal_name: Positivity of Degree Bound in Chevalley's Theorem
items.type: ∀ (k : ℕ) (D : ℕ → ℕ) (n : ℕ), 0 < ChevalleyThm.MvPolynomialC.degBound k D n
items.informal_description: For any natural number $k$ and function $D : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$, the degree bound $\text{degBound}\,k\,D\,n$ satisfies $0 < \text{degBound}\,k\,D\,n$ for all $n \in \mathbb{N}$.

items.informal_name: Degree Bound for Multivariate Polynomials in Chevalley's Theorem
items.informal_description: A function that computes a degree bound for multivariate polynomials, taking a natural number $n$, a function $f : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$, and an element of the sum type $\mathbb{N} \oplus \mathbb{N}$. For left components, it applies $f$ to $n$, and for right components, it returns $n$ directly. This is used in the proof of Chevalley's theorem to establish well-founded recursion for multivariate polynomial constructions.

items.informal_name: Existence of Polynomial Pairs with Bounded Degree Difference
items.type:
∀ {Fq : Type u_1} [inst : Fintype Fq] [inst_1 : Ring Fq] {d m : ℕ},
  Fintype.card Fq ^ d ≤ m →
    ∀ (b : Polynomial Fq) (A : Fin m.succ → Polynomial Fq),
      (∀ (i : Fin m.succ), (A i).degree < b.degree) → ∃ i₀ i₁, i₀ ≠ i₁ ∧ (A i₁ - A i₀).degree < ↑(b.natDegree - d)
items.informal_description: Given a finite ring $ Fq $ with cardinality $ q $, natural numbers $ d $ and $ m $ such that $ q^d \leq m $, a nonzero polynomial $ b \in Fq[X] $, and a function $ A: \mathrm{Fin}(m+1) \to Fq[X] $ where each $ A(i) $ has degree less than $ \deg(b) $, there exist distinct indices $ i_0, i_1 \in \mathrm{Fin}(m+1) $ such that the degree of $ A(i_1) - A(i_0) $ satisfies $ \deg(A(i_1) - A(i_0)) < \mathrm{natdeg}(b) - d $, where $ \mathrm{natdeg}(b) $ denotes the natural degree of $ b $ (equal to $ \deg(b) $ if nonzero, otherwise 0).

items.informal_name: Combinatorial Nullstellensatz: Existence of Non-Vanishing Evaluation
items.type:
∀ {R : Type u_1} [inst : CommRing R] {σ : Type u_2} [Finite σ] [IsDomain R] (f : MvPolynomial σ R) (t : σ →₀ ℕ),
  MvPolynomial.coeff t f ≠ 0 →
    f.totalDegree = Finsupp.degree t →
      ∀ (S : σ → Finset R), (∀ (i : σ), t i < (S i).card) → ∃ s, (∀ (i : σ), s i ∈ S i) ∧ (MvPolynomial.eval s) f ≠ 0
items.informal_description: Let $ R $ be an integral domain, $ f $ a multivariate polynomial in $ R[\sigma] $, and $ t $ a monomial with nonzero coefficient in $ f $ such that the total degree of $ f $ equals the degree of $ t $. For any family of finite subsets $ S_i \subseteq R $ indexed by $ \sigma $, if each $ S_i $ has cardinality strictly greater than the exponent of $ t $ in variable $ i $, then there exists an evaluation $ s : \sigma \to R $ with $ s(i) \in S_i $ for all $ i $, such that $ f(s) \neq 0 $. This is the combinatorial Nullstellensatz existence theorem.

items.informal_description: The set of all functions $ v $ for which $ f(v) \neq g(v) $ forms a Diophantine set, meaning there exists a polynomial equation with integer coefficients such that $ f(v) \neq g(v) $ holds if and only if the equation is solvable in additional variables.

items.informal_name: Degree of Variable in Polynomial Difference is Less Than k Under Coefficient Equality Conditions
items.type:
∀ {R : Type u} {σ : Type u_1} [inst : CommRing R] {x : σ} {f g : MvPolynomial σ R} {k : ℕ},
  0 < k →
    (∀ m ∈ f.support, k ≤ m x → MvPolynomial.coeff m f = MvPolynomial.coeff m g) →
      (∀ m ∈ g.support, k ≤ m x → MvPolynomial.coeff m f = MvPolynomial.coeff m g) → MvPolynomial.degreeOf x (f - g) < k
items.informal_description: For a variable $x$ in $\sigma$ and polynomials $f, g \in R[\sigma]$, if for all monomials $m$ with non-zero coefficients in $f$ or $g$, the coefficients of $m$ in $f$ and $g$ are equal whenever the exponent of $x$ in $m$ is at least $k$, then the total degree of $x$ in $f - g$ is strictly less than $k$.
